# TOSCA ZSM-5 experiment — results dashboard

**RB 2620468 · H-ZSM-5, Si/Al ≈ 140**

These plots use the **full measured TOSCA grid: 888 data points per spectrum between 20 and 1700 cm⁻¹. No spectral points are discarded or averaged for the dashboard.**

## Processing used here

- Loaded ZSM-5 samples: agreed smoothed empty-ZSM-5 subtraction.
- Empty-ZSM-5 smoothing: 5 points to 500 cm⁻¹, gradually increasing to 8 points by 4500 cm⁻¹.
- Pure methanol: small empty Al-can subtraction.
- Pure 1-propanol: large empty Al-can subtraction currently available.
- Each spectrum is normalized independently to its first main low-frequency peak in 40–200 cm⁻¹.
- Vertical offsets are display-only.
- Main range: 20–1700 cm⁻¹.

### Note on the original 2.13 wt% run

The gravimetric loading is retained as **2.13 wt%**. Not all of the sample was positioned in front of the neutron beam, so its **absolute intensity is not reliable**. Because each trace is normalized independently, it remains useful for **spectral-shape comparison**.

The main caveat is background subtraction: the altered sample/beam overlap changes the relative Al-frame and zeolite contributions compared with the empty-ZSM-5 measurement. The **Aluminium-can subtraction is therefore less reliable for this trace**, especially where the Al contribution is appreciable.

The 7.86 wt% 1-propanol run is retained for spectral-shape comparison, but its absolute amplitude is not trusted because only part of the sample was in the beam.

## Experimental caveats

- The Al foil frame can contribute a slightly different amplitude from run to run.
- The original 2.13 wt% MeOH and 7.86 wt% 1-propanol runs had sample-positioning problems.
- For those runs, normalization makes shape comparison useful, but **background/can subtraction is less secure**.
- No fitted Al or beam-overlap correction is applied on this basic dashboard.
- The normalized plots are therefore intended primarily for **shape comparison**, not quantitative comparison of absolute INS intensity.
